question: Can CodeForge complete a real engineering task through the canonical completion authority evaluateCompletion on a real free provider route?
answer: YES — proven on the digest-locked tiny task qual-js-return-sign.

harness.design: Drives the production WorkflowService → WorkflowEngine → AgentRuntime path (same code the packaged server uses), not an AgentRuntime-only slice. Success criterion is the workflow's own completion-gated terminal state plus an independent hidden verifier.

bounds.requestCeiling: R28_LIVE_MAX_REQUESTS (default 24, hard max 60) enforced by bounded adapter
bounds.outputCeiling: R28_LIVE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (default 512, hard max 1024); a provider-reported breach blocks any further dispatch
bounds.freeOnly: FREE_API providers with zero declared paid spillover; route must report verified_free in the live catalog; ForgeZero firewall registered
bounds.workspace: disposable temp copy of the digest-locked fixture; deleted unless R28_LIVE_KEEP_WORKSPACE=true
bounds.spend: no request is ever sent unless R28_LIVE_ENABLE=true

harness.authority: TaskAuthority lease permissionMode=full_autonomy planMode=auto (a real product mode). Plan auto-approved via policy receipt; tier-3/4 actions still escalate.

authorityReceipts.note: One tier-3 action correctly escalated to ask and went unanswered; the agent adapted and completed anyway — permission enforcement held under live conditions.

gapClosed: R27 Gap 2 (canonical live task completion) is closed at tiny scale. The R27 run ended blocked at a 4-turn AgentRuntime budget before the workflow gate; R28 drove the actual workflow to the gate.
notProven: packaged live completion through the installed product
